meta.name: Deploy curated Docker app stacks to a Hostinger VPS via forms and email

parameters.content:
## Deploy a curated Docker app stack to a Hostinger VPS from a form

### How it works

This workflow deploys a Docker-based stack to a selected Hostinger VPS using a guided form flow. It lists available VPS instances, lets the user choose a target and provide deployment metadata, creates the Docker project, waits for the Hostinger action status, and branches into success or failure handling. On success, it collects container information and emails a stack summary; on failure, it retrieves logs and formats a failure summary.

### Setup steps

- Configure Hostinger API credentials for all Hostinger API nodes.
- Configure the email sending credentials used by the Send Stack Summary Email node.
- Review the form fields so they collect the required stack label, notification email, and VPS selection inputs.
- Update the code nodes that build VPS options, deployment items, action unwrapping, status parsing, and summary email content to match the desired Docker stack and Hostinger API response shape.
- Set an appropriate wait duration in the Wait for Deployment node so the deployment has enough time before status is checked.

### Customization

Customize the Docker project payload, polling delay, success email template, and failure summary formatting. If failure notifications are required, connect the failure branch to an email or alerting node.

## Start and list VPS

Captures the initial stack deployment request and retrieves the available VPS instances from Hostinger, then prepares them as options for the next form.

## Select deployment target

Shows the VPS selection form and normalizes the chosen virtual machine, stack label, and notification email into fields used downstream.

## Create Docker project

Builds the deployment payload, creates the Docker project through the Hostinger API, and extracts the returned action details for status tracking.

## Check deployment status

Waits for the deployment action to progress, fetches its status from Hostinger, unwraps the response, and branches based on whether deployment succeeded.

## Format successful app

On a successful deployment, lists Docker containers for the project and formats the application details into a success summary block.

## Format failed deployment

On a failed deployment, retrieves Docker project logs and formats the stack label, notification email, and failure summary for review.

## Email deployment summary

Aggregates formatted success output, builds a stack summary email, and sends it to the configured notification recipient.

const LABEL_TO_KEY = {"Developer Stack": "developer", "Hobbyist Stack": "hobbyist", "Freelancer Stack": "freelancer", "AI/LLM Stack": "ai-llm"};

const cfg = $input.first().json;
const stackKey = LABEL_TO_KEY[cfg.stackLabel];
if (!stackKey) {
  throw new Error(`Unknown stack selection: ${cfg.stackLabel}`);
}
const appSlugs = CATALOG.stacks[stackKey];

function randomToken(len) {
  const chars = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
  let out = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
    out += chars[Math.floor(Math.random() * chars.length)];
  }
  return out;
}

const items = [];
for (const slug of appSlugs) {
  const app = CATALOG.apps[slug];
  let content = app.compose;
  const generatedSecrets = {};
  for (const secretName of app.secrets) {
    const token = `__${secretName}__`;
    const value = randomToken(20);
    generatedSecrets[secretName] = value;
    content = content.split(token).join(value);
  }
  items.push({
    json: {
      virtualMachineId: cfg.virtualMachineId,
      notifyEmail: cfg.notifyEmail,
      stackKey: stackKey,
      stackLabel: cfg.stackLabel,
      slug: slug,
      displayName: app.display_name,
      projectName: `${stackKey}-${slug}`.slice(0, 64),
      content: content,
      hostPorts: app.host_ports.join(', '),
      appNotes: app.notes,
      generatedSecrets: generatedSecrets,
    }
  });
}
return items;
